title: Demobilization, Recovery & Responder Resilience
learningObjectives: Demobilize resources safely and reconcile every patient.
Run a hot wash and contribute to an after-action review.
Apply responder rehab and Psychological First Aid.
Recognize stress reactions that need referral.

summary.title: Demobilization Is an Operation
summary.content: Release resources as they're no longer needed, not all at once — keep enough for re-triage, late-found patients, and responder rehab. Each unit is checked out: crew accounted for, rehab/medical check, equipment decontaminated (CBRNE), restocked, returned to service. Command is formally terminated and announced. Before closing: reconcile the patient count — scene tags = transport log = hospital arrivals (+ dead + released on scene). A mismatch means someone is missing.

summary.title: Documentation That Matters
summary.content: MCI paperwork is short but non-negotiable: triage tags (they ARE records), the transport log, unit assignments, times, tourniquet times, antidotes and decon given, and exposure logs for responders (chemical/radiological/biological). Complete abbreviated or full ePCRs per local policy after the incident. Records drive reunification, legal review, reimbursement, and the after-action report.

summary.title: Hot Wash & After-Action Review
summary.content: HOT WASH: within minutes–hours, short, informal, everyone present: what went well, what didn't, any immediate safety issues. AFTER-ACTION REVIEW/REPORT (AAR) with an Improvement Plan: What was supposed to happen? What actually happened? Why was there a difference? What do we sustain, what do we improve — with owners and deadlines. Blame-free and systems-focused. Feed lessons into plans, training, and drills (tabletop → functional → full-scale exercises).

summary.title: Responder Rehab
summary.content: Rehab starts during the incident, not after: shade/shelter, hydration, food, rest, medical monitoring (vitals, symptoms, CO if smoke exposure). Rotate crews before exhaustion — e.g., NFPA 1584 guidance: rehab after two 30-minute SCBA cylinders or ~40 minutes of intense work. Watch for heat illness, rhabdomyolysis, chest pain, and dehydration in your own people.

summary.title: Psychological First Aid, Not Forced Debriefing
summary.content: Stress reactions (poor sleep, intrusive images, irritability, numbness) are common and usually fade in days to weeks. Psychological First Aid (PFA) — 'Look, Listen, Link': ensure safety and basic needs, listen without pushing for details, connect to social support and services. Mandatory single-session psychological debriefing (forcing everyone to relive the event) is NOT recommended — it doesn't prevent PTSD and may harm. Use peer support, buddy checks, and follow-up; refer when symptoms persist beyond ~a month, worsen, or include suicidal thoughts or substance misuse.

clinicalPearls: Tags + transport log + hospital list must add up. If they don't, keep looking.
Release units in phases — the last patients are often found after the scene 'feels' over.
The hot wash is for facts and safety, not therapy — keep it short.
Look, Listen, Link: PFA works for colleagues as well as patients.
Normal people have strong reactions to abnormal events — say it out loud to your crew.
redFlags: A colleague who can't sleep, drinks more, or withdraws weeks after the incident.
Any responder talking about hopelessness or self-harm — act today.
Patient numbers that don't reconcile with hospitals.
Contaminated equipment returned to service without decon.
commonMistakes: Releasing all resources the moment the last red is transported.
Skipping the hot wash because 'everyone is tired'.
Forcing all staff into a single group debrief to 'process' the event.
Writing AAR findings without owners or deadlines — nothing changes.
memoryAids: Demob: Check out, Clean, Restock, Return.
AAR 4 questions: Supposed to? Actually? Why different? Sustain/Improve?
Reconcile: Tags = Log = Hospitals (+ dead + released).

decisionTrees.title: Closing the Incident
decisionTrees.content:
All patients transported/released?
  → Reconcile counts: tags = transport log = hospital arrivals (+ dead/released)
     → Mismatch: search, re-check hospitals, re-sweep scene
  → Phased demob: rehab check → decon → restock → return to service
  → Terminate command (announce)
  → Hot wash today → AAR/Improvement Plan → update plans & training
  → PFA + peer follow-up for responders; refer persistent symptoms

references: FEMA HSEEP — After-Action Report / Improvement Plan
WHO Psychological First Aid: Guide for Field Workers (Look, Listen, Link)
NFPA 1584 — Rehabilitation Process for Members During Emergency Operations
Cochrane/WHO guidance on single-session psychological debriefing
